cells.tense: You are choosing this right now, and the choosing is not scraping you out.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are still choosing on purpose, say it out loud to somebody tonight, then let tomorrow take its own run at it.
cells.core:
You picked a direction and you are still walking it. Nothing has knocked you loose — the aim held through the stretch where it stopped being exciting, and you don't make a speech about that. That is the good part.

The same talent has a dull edge, and it is worth knowing where. Staying has made you loyal to the course past the point of checking it; you pick up the same aim out of habit instead of deciding again. A steadiness that doesn't look up can keep steering a road you would not choose today.

Pick one thing that should carry on exactly as it is, and say who you are keeping it for. Anything else can wait until you mean it again.
cells.sheetLine: You chose this and you're still choosing it. Say so out loud.

cells.tense: You are already standing inside a moment that has not arrived, bracing for the part you cannot write.
cells.ask: Take one plan you are bracing over and turn it into a question, then put something on the table today that you can see.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead the whole thing works, the people around you understand, and the waiting ends — and you are living there instead of here. So moves get made early, gaps get filled before anyone asks, and you call it persistence. Same aim, throttle jammed.

What the force is protecting is the direction itself, and that part is fine. Nothing has ended. You just can't stand the stretch where the outcome sits outside your hands, and waiting looks like doing nothing.

Before the next push, take one thing you are pressing on and leave it alone for a day. If it falls over without you, that tells you something about it. If it stands, that tells you something better.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that has been behind you for a while now.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you stopped pushing last year and tend it small this week — fifteen minutes, only the piece you still care about.
cells.core:
The direction is still in view somewhere; the hand that steered it isn't on the wheel. Decisions here come late, get made by whoever else is in the room, and get called fine. The thing is still wanted. The acting like it stopped.

You keep coming back to it in the abstract and you stopped pitching in. That is ground to be tended, not a mood to wait on.

One low-stakes piece of it, this week, before the question is settled anywhere. Enough to find out whether the care is still warm. That kind of answer comes from practice, not from courage.

Nothing about the ask depends on this reading being right. Tend one small piece and you will know more either way.
cells.sheetLine: Someday starts with one small piece, this week.

cells.tense: You are steering already, and you keep describing the steering as if it were weather.
cells.ask: For one decision you keep calling inevitable, write three lines of what you actually want before you answer anybody about it.
cells.core:
Nobody is making you keep going at this. That's you, and you've been at it long enough that it feels like conditions — the industry is slow, the timing is off, the season is wrong. Some of that is even true. It also isn't the whole account, and your thumb is on it.

Once the steering gets said out loud as yours, you can steer harder or set it down. Either one works. What doesn't work is the version where it happens to you, because then there is nothing to reshape.

Before the next update you give somebody, make your own shorthand first: what you want, what you will do, what you are leaving open. Fifteen minutes and a corner of the page.

attempts.check: The record establishes a capacity — directed choosing — and its condition, not a history, so any line that supplies a reason for the Too Little state (a costly moment, a loss, a person) is unsupported and was cut; the Too Little core now only reports conduct a person could recognise. The reader could reasonably say the bracing described in Too Much is just diligence, and the withdrawing described in Too Little is just a season of low energy, so both cores lean on what can be seen from outside and leave the motive alone. The asks survive being wrong about the status: naming one deliberate choice, turning one plan into a question, tending one small piece, writing three lines before replying — each is finishable today, needs nobody else, costs nothing, and teaches something about steering whatever the read was.
